acceptance: test_canary_impact_live passes in a shallow clone without requiring historical commit objects.
test_no_cli_surface_drift either receives its base ref cleanly or skips with an explicit message rather than silently dropping its gate or hard-failing on merge-base.
test_ledger_seed does not trigger an unbounded git fetch of published-results at import time during test collection.
Running the three test files in a shallow clone (git clone --depth 1 file://$PWD) passes with zero unexplained failures or new skips.
context: Part of the shallow-clone CI optimization plan. Audit identified these three tests as the blockers preventing medium-test shards (which run 4 shards × 25m each) and medium-collect from using shallow checkouts. Once remediated, medium tiers can be converted to depth 1.
description: Three tests currently fail or trigger unbounded network fetches in shallow checkouts: (1) tests/unit/test_canary_impact_live.py runs git diff against hard-coded commit SHAs; (2) tests/uat/test_no_cli_surface_drift.py needs origin/develop and runs merge-base against it; (3) tests/unit/scripts/publication/test_ledger_seed.py runs git cat-file on a recorded commit at import time and falls back to an unbounded git fetch of published-results. Fix or isolate these tests: replace hard-coded commit diffs with frozen fixtures, define a clear base-ref contract for the CLI surface drift test, and pre-fetch the specific recorded commit or guard the import-time fetch in test_ledger_seed. This unblocks shallow checkouts for medium-test shards and test collection.
